newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Maverick Nigerian musician gives Abacha thumbs up.
newsitem.headline: Maverick Nigerian musician gives Abacha thumbs up.

text.p: Nigerian Afro-beat superstar Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, an ardent critic of military rule, made a volte- face in an interview published on Thursday, urging military ruler General Sani Abacha to stay on as the nation's president.
"Abacha is the best head of state to rule this country so far," Fela said in the interview with the opposition weekly magazine Tempo.
"If Abacha no go wetin them fit do? To me oh! make he stay," he said in his trademark pidgin English meaning:"If Abacha does not give up power what can people do? To me let him stay on."

Abacha, who seized power in chaos unleashed when a presidential poll was annulled in 1993, says he will hand over in October 1998 to a democratically-elected president and there is widespread belief that he will contest the election.
In the 1970s and 1980s, Fela, who is now aged 59, produced music which featured songs that abused soldiers and portrayed them as being of low intelligence.
But since the 1990s he has kept to himself at his Lagos home and performs occasionally at his club, called "The Shrine."
Fela, who has a reputation for smoking marijuana openly and dressing only in underpants, was detained with 30 of his band a year ago by anti-narcotics agents after a swoop on his home.
They were later released but Fela was handed to the narcotic agency's counselling unit for therapy sessions.
The musician formed a political party in 1979 which was disqualified from the elections at that time.
"No! No! I don't have interest in politics again," he told Tempo.
His brother Beko Ransome-Kuti, a pro-democracy campaigner, was jailed for 15 years in 1995 for alleged involvement in a plot to topple Abacha's government.
